claims.text: The starting CoCrFeNi alloy is a single-phase high-entropy alloy.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits elevated friction at high temperatures.
Unmodified CoCrFeNi exhibits elevated wear at high temperatures.
Incorporating a suitable precursor into CoCrFeNi will induce an in situ self-lubricating phase under sliding and high-temperature conditions.
The precursor-derived lubricious phase will be nanoscale.
The intervention will form a nanoscale tribofilm or dispersed lubricious phase at the sliding interface.
Contact stress and thermal activation will cause the precursor to react or transform during sliding.
The precursor transformation will generate a stable lubricious phase that forms a protective tribofilm.
The lubricious phase will provide a low-shear interface.
Providing a low-shear interface will reduce friction.
The protective tribofilm will reduce wear.
The lubricious film will remain resilient from room temperature to 800 °C.
Modified CoCrFeNi will have a significantly lower coefficient of friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
Modified CoCrFeNi will have lower wear rates than unmodified CoCrFeNi across the full room-temperature-to-800 °C range.
The self-generated lubricious phase will continuously replenish during operation.
The beneficial effect will persist under moderate to high contact pressures.
The beneficial effect will persist in oxidizing environments typical of high-temperature sliding.
The beneficial effect may degrade under extreme mechanical loads or highly aggressive chemical environments.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts low friction and reduced wear across the full temperature range, but the falsification rule only requires a greater-than-20% reduction across 'most' of the range. Thus, failure at one or more temperatures could contradict the full-range prediction without falsifying the hypothesis.
